text.insert: A PR campaign converts one stable point into a set of reviewable series and shepherds them through the upstream review cycle. Review latency is external and long — reviewers are volunteers with their own queues — so the campaign is durable and mostly dormant: remote observation and feedback ingestion advance series in the background, while publication, fixing, and validation execute only inside lease-holding activations. The campaign is also where the agent learns: review outcomes are processed into standards and knowledge before the next run consumes them.

props.title: Decision (2026-08-11) — PR work is an operator-entered phase, never a preemption

text.insert: Review feedback that arrives during an active run is ingested immediately as durable PR work items and surfaced in the operator projection, but fixer execution waits until the operator activates PR work. PR authority normally follows run completion; an operator who needs it mid-run must explicitly trigger a handoff that drains the run at the current epoch boundary.
How PR Work Yields to a Run

Evidence ingestion is background-safe, so PR authority can wait for the run to finish rather than interrupt it. The normal sequence is to run for however long is useful, reach a stable point, split the results into PRs, and then work a review cycle that usually takes about a week.
Running PR work and run processing at the same time is an explicitly desired future relaxation:
PR workspaces share no mutable state with the session source, so the single-active-workflow rule is a worker-capacity and simplicity constraint rather than a source-truth requirement.
v1 nevertheless keeps exactly one dispatch-lease holder; any later concurrency must revisit this decision instead of silently weakening the lease.

props.title: Decision (2026-08-12) — one durable PrCampaign spans the review cycle

text.insert: PR work uses one durable campaign per split of a stable point, and v1 keeps at most one campaign open at a time. The campaign spans the full review cycle and holds the dispatch lease only during operator-entered activations that publish, fix, or validate.
Why One Campaign at a Time
A campaign is durable because it persists across the whole multi-week review cycle, but it is mostly dormant:
Remote observation and feedback ingestion advance series in the background, while operator-entered activations publish, fix, or validate.
An activation is the period in which the campaign holds the dispatch lease for that work, and each one lands as a pr_phase entry in the session timeline.
Publication is operator-gated and opens series in batches of around four so reviewers are never handed ten sweeping PRs at once; the remaining series stay prepared until an explicit go.
The campaign is where the agent learns whether it did things correctly:
Review outcomes become standards and knowledge.
A campaign therefore normally runs to conclusion before the next run produces the next batch, because overlapping campaigns would interleave learning from two baselines.
Runs during a campaign remain possible through the explicit handoff in the PR-phase decision above, but they are not the expected pattern.
